research_depth.summary: Both language editions exceed 5,000 substantive words, with distinct historical, institutional and conditional sections.

evidence_traceability.summary: TSE's 21:26 official live source cross-checked, first-round TSE figures, 2026 Chamber composition, US National Archives and Library of Congress, USTR, WTO, IMF, World Bank, IBGE and MDIC.

counterfactual_review.summary: Domestic agency versus external influence, coalition outcomes and conditional 2027-2030 paths distinguished; projections are not represented as observed outcomes.

visual_evidence_readiness.summary: Both editions have a table, three quantitative charts, a regional map, causal flows and a mindmap. Chart series are identical.

editorial_style.summary: Substantive historical narrative with documented claims, alternative interpretations and no operational product instructions.

source_review.summary: Source-linked factual checks performed, including direct TSE official data read at 99.87% of sections; sampled URLs from sources in different domains.

bilingual_parity.summary: All numerical sequences and dated evidence limitations matched; 2026 election-night Datafolha snapshot and later TSE count separately labeled.

institutional_integrity.summary: Explicit distinction among election forecast, mathematically irreversible count, completed tally and formal certification.

contrary_evidence: Flávio Bolsonaro led the official 4 October first-round count; the subsequent runoff reversal cannot be assigned to one cause without voter-level evidence.
Brazil's 2026 congressional results create conservative veto points that constrain the president's governing ability.
US-Brazil trade and technological cooperation coexists with historically documented intervention and current tariff disputes.
limitations: Final 100% of the 25 October runoff was not available at the reporting cutoff; all second-round percentages are timestamped provisional results.
The TSE JSON is a live official file and can change after the quoted timestamp; values are explicitly documented in both reports.
Regional vote patterns and voter motivation require further official final-data and empirical analysis.
Historic international involvement should not be treated as evidence of a foreign actor controlling the 2026 election.
notes: Editorial fact/structure review conducted in-session with cross-checks against the referenced sources. Not claimed as external academic peer review. No unverified allegations of 2026 electoral fraud are asserted.
